title: Function Plot Slider Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mathematics; Data Visualization
description: Interactive Plotly.js function plot in which a slider moves a red marker along sin(x), cos(x), x squared or e^(-x^2), a readout reports x and f(x), and a Show matches button marks every x where the curve reaches a target output.

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will locate the x values where a chosen function reaches a given output, by moving a marker along the curve and reading the tooltip.
prerequisites: The idea of a function and its graph
Familiarity with sine, cosine, squares and exponentials

simulation.model: Sampled function plot with a movable marker and root finding for f(x) = target

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Move a marker, read the readout, check with Show matches
keyQuestions: How many x values in the domain give sin(x) = 0.5, and why?
Why does e^(-x^2) = 2 have no solution?
commonMisconceptions: An equation such as sin(x) = 0.5 has only one solution.
A curve that touches a level without crossing it does not reach that level.
assessmentOpportunities: Locate all x values where a function reaches a target to within 0.01
Explain differing match counts from the shape of each curve
